title: Playbook serialization, safe autopatch runner, and compact incident snapshot format
author: Marco Chen
release_notes: Adds compact playbook snapshot format for faster on-call handoffs; implements a gated autopatch runner (dry-run, canary, production with approval); exposes metrics for playbook serialization and autopatch attempts; includes migration tool to backfill legacy runbooks.
description:
Title: Playbook serialization, safe autopatch runner, and compact incident snapshot format

Summary: This PR introduces a compact, versioned serialization format for on-call playbooks and incident snapshots (ndjson-lite), a gated 'autopatch' runner that can apply recommended mitigations with dry-run and canary modes, and a small migration utility that backfills existing runbooks into the new snapshot format. The goal is to make handoffs and automated remediation faster and safer: snapshots are smaller on disk, deserialize faster in the UI/CLI, and autopatch requires configurable approval gates before affecting production resources.

Context & motivation: During post-incident reviews and regular on-call workflows we observed two recurring pain points: (1) large serialized playbooks (with full telemetry attachments) were slow to fetch and caused UI lag during handoff, and (2) teams wanted a safer path to attempt automated mitigations without risking blind writes in production. This change addresses both by providing a compact snapshot for fast handoff and a conservative autopatch runner with explicit dry-run/canary/approve semantics. Related Linear: ENG-1249 (playbook serialization), ENG-1350 (autopatch safety). Related support ticket: SUP-4421 (customer request for safer auto-remediation).

What changed (high level):
- New serialization module incident_bot.playbook.serialize implementing a compact NDJSON-like snapshot (versioned schema v2). Snapshots include compacted steps, pointer references to large attachments, and optionally inlined thumbnails.
- Autopatch runner incident_bot.autopatch that supports: dry-run mode (no writes), canary mode (apply to a subset of targets, default 1%), and production mode which requires 2 approvals for sensitive namespaces. The runner logs intent, a proposed patch diff, and emits a signed intent token.
- CLI flags: `ibctl snapshot export --compact` and `ibctl autopatch run --mode=canary` plus `--approvals=2` override.
- Migration script tools/migrate_playbooks_to_v2.py to backfill existing DB playbooks into v2 snapshots; this runs in batches and has idempotent checkpoints.
- Observability: new metrics incidentbot.playbook.serialize_ms, incidentbot.autopatch.attempts_total, incidentbot.autopatch.success_total, and associated tracing spans. Added Grafana dashboard snippets in observability/dashboards/playbook-autopatch.json.
- Tests: unit tests for serialization edge cases, integration test for autopatch dry-run and canary modes, and a local e2e test that exercises the CLI export/import flow.

Review thread (high level):
- Aisha Patel (review): Asked for clearer schema versioning and a migration rollback plan; flagged potential security concerns around signed intent tokens and token rotation.
  - Author response: Added schema version field and a migration checkpoint/rollback step in tools/migrate_playbooks_to_v2.py; rotated token signing keys to use KMS and required token TTL.
- Dmitri Volkov (review): Requested stricter default canary percentage (changed to 1% -> 0.5% for high-sensitivity namespaces), and asked to add a safelist for low-risk namespaces.
  - Author response: Implemented per-namespace risk profiles with default 0.5% for high-risk, 5% for low-risk; added config file autopatch/config.yaml to house safelist.
- Nora Kim (approver): Asked for CI evidence showing integration test flakiness addressed; requested a follow-up task to add chaos tests.
  - Author response: Fixed a race in test harness (sleep -> event wait), re-ran CI and added a follow-up Linear task ENG-1401 to add chaos testing to the autopatch pipeline.

CI summary:
- Initial CI run: lint=pass, unit tests=pass, integration tests=fail (flaky harness race discovered), e2e=not run by default; fixed in branch with test harness change.
- Subsequent CI run: lint=pass, unit tests=pass, integration tests=pass, e2e=pass (local e2e in CI matrix), coverage maintained (no regression). All checks green at merge.

Backward compatibility & safety notes:
- Snapshots are versioned; the system can read v1 and v2. The new serializer defaults to v2 for exports but import path will accept v1 and v2.
- Autopatch defaults to dry-run for all users; production application requires explicit approval flow (two approvers for sensitive namespaces). Admins can opt in to relax policies per workspace.
- Migration script is opt-in and includes idempotent checkpoints and a dry-run reporting mode.

Performance impact:
- Snapshot size reduced ~30% on median playbook (measured across 1200 samples); serialization time reduced ~40% in benchmark harness.
- Autopatch runner adds minimal overhead during plan creation; execution path optimized to batch target updates where supported by downstream providers.

Follow-ups / future work:
- ENG-1401: add chaos/resilience tests for autopatch pipeline.
- ENG-1418: integrate snapshot diff view into the Console incident handoff UX.
- Explore signed snapshot exchange protocol for cross-team handoffs (design doc in docs/handbook).

Merge outcome: Squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-26 after approvals from Nora Kim and Dmitri Volkov. All CI checks passing at the time of merge.

Notes for release: This change is non-breaking by default; operators should review the migration tool before running it in production. Recommend announcing the autopatch feature to SRE teams with a runbook that documents approval flows and safelist configuration.
